items.q: Scissors reflex on retinoscopy with irregular astigmatism in a teenager most suggests what?
o: Keratoconus needing topography and crosslinking assessment
items.exp: Irregular cone optics split the reflex; topography confirms and crosslinking stiffens progressive disease while spectacles fail. Allergic eye rubbing accelerates cones.
items.kp: Scissors reflex in teen: cone the cornea.

items.q: Munson sign in keratoconus refers to what?
o: Lower lid bulge on downgaze from the cone
items.exp: The cone indents the lid in downgaze; Vogt striae and Fleischer rings complete bedside signs before topography quantifies. Acute hydrops instead clouds suddenly with pain.
r: Correct. Lid bulge on looking down.
items.kp: Cone dents lid looking down: Munson.

items.q: Sudden painful corneal clouding with tearing in known keratoconus is which emergency?
o: Acute hydrops from Descemet tear needing hyperosmotics and later graft assessment
items.exp: Descemet rupture floods stroma with aqueous; most settle over weeks leaving scars, with intracameral gas or keratoplasty for non resolving or scarred cases. Steroids alone never seal tears.
r: Incorrect. No graft exists to reject.
Correct. Hydrops, dry then judge scar.
items.kp: Cone suddenly milky and sore: hydrops tore Descemet.

items.q: Morning blurring clearing through the day with guttae in a 60 year old indicates what?
o: Fuchs endothelial dystrophy progressing to bullous keratopathy
items.exp: Failing pumps swell stroma overnight; hypertonic drops temporise and endothelial keratoplasty restores when bullae rupture painfully. Cataract blurs constantly.
r: Incorrect. Lens blur ignores time of day.
items.kp: Dawn blur fading by lunch: Fuchs endothelium.

items.q: Arcus senilis before age forty should prompt testing for what?
items.exp: Premature lipid keratopathy reflects systemic dyslipidaemia with vascular risk; senile arcus with lucid interval is otherwise benign ageing. Xanthelasma companions strengthen the hunt.

items.q: Horizontal calcium band across interpalpebral cornea in chronic uveitis is what and removed how?
items.exp: Calcium deposits in Bowman membrane with lucid interval near limbus; chelation lifts it improving vision and comfort while uveitis control prevents return. Phosphate drops precipitate it.
items.kp: Chalk band in chronic uveitis: chelate calcium.

items.q: Lattice dystrophy is distinguished by which features?
o: Refractile branching lines with recurrent painful erosions and amyloid deposits
items.exp: Amyloid lines fracture epithelium causing waking pain and erosions; hypertonics and bandage lenses bridge, with transplant for scarring. Granular dystrophy instead crumbs without early erosions.
items.kp: Branching lines plus waking pain: lattice.

items.q: Kayser Fleischer ring differs from Fleischer ring by which pair?
o: Copper in Descemet signalling Wilson disease versus iron at keratoconus cone base
items.exp: Slit lamp separates brown Descemet copper in youth with hepatic or movement signs from rusty epithelial iron encircling cones; penicillamine pathways follow Wilson confirmation.
items.kp: Brown Descemet ring plus tremor: Wilson copper.

items.q: Corneal crosslinking is indicated to do what in keratoconus?
o: Halt progression by stiffening stroma with riboflavin and ultraviolet light
items.exp: Crosslinks freeze cone steepening in documented progressors (often youth); vision rehabilitation still needs contact lenses or later grafting for scars. Endothelium minimum thickness guards safety.
items.kp: Crosslink young cones to freeze them.

items.q: Limbal stem cell deficiency after chemical burns presents how and needs what?
o: Conjunctivalisation with vessels and persistent defects needing stem cell or amniotic reconstruction
items.exp: Destroyed palisades cannot resurface cornea so conjunctiva invades; standard grafts fail without stem support, requiring limbal transplantation before optical grafting.
items.kp: Burnt limbus grows conjunctiva: replace stems first.
